findings.evidence: Convergence.lean:66-81 vs 87-102: identical hypothesis lists; the only difference is `(x : A.domain)` vs `(x : X)` and the coercion in the statement.
findings.fix: Delete `..._of_pow_le_of_mem`; consumers use `exp_yosidaApproximation_uniformCauchySeqOn_compact_of_pow_le hM hres hpow hdense (x : X) hT`. If a domain-vector spelling is wanted, prove it by exactly that term rather than by a second call into `..._compact_of_mem`.
findings.issue: `exp_yosidaApproximation_uniformCauchySeqOn_compact_of_pow_le_of_mem` has exactly the same hypotheses (hM, hres, hpow, hdense, hT) as `exp_yosidaApproximation_uniformCauchySeqOn_compact_of_pow_le` in the same file, and its conclusion is that lemma applied to `(x : X)`. Unlike the Yosida.lean pair (where the whole-space version is proved from the domain version), neither is used to prove the other here, so the domain version adds nothing.

findings.evidence: grep of `hA.norm_resolvent_le` shows the identical `by simpa [one_div]` discharge at LimitSemigroup.lean:124, 137 and LumerPhillips.lean:86; `norm_exp_smul_yosidaApproximation_le_one (hA.mul_norm_resolvent_le_one h) h hs` at LimitSemigroup.lean:125-126 and 138-139.
findings.fix: Restore the three `IsMDissipative.*` one-line specializations in Yosida.lean (each `:= general_lemma (fun _ h => hA.mem_resolventSet h) (fun _ h => by simpa [one_div] using hA.norm_resolvent_le h) ... hdense ...`) and call them at LimitSemigroup.lean:121, 134 and LumerPhillips.lean:84.
findings.issue: The m-dissipative instantiation block `(K := 1) (M := 1) (fun _ h => hA.mem_resolventSet h) (fun _ h => by simpa [one_div] using hA.norm_resolvent_le h) (fun _ h _ hs => norm_exp_smul_yosidaApproximation_le_one (hA.mul_norm_resolvent_le_one h) h hs)` is repeated verbatim at LimitSemigroup.lean:121-126 and 134-139, and its resolvent half again at LumerPhillips.lean:84-86. The PR description claims `IsMDissipative.tendsto_smul_resolvent_apply_atTop`, `.tendsto_yosidaApproximation_apply_atTop` and `.exp_yosidaApproximation_uniformCauchySeqOn_compact` were kept as one-line specializations, but they were deleted, so each call site re-derives the same specialization.

findings.evidence: grep `nonneg_of_norm_resolvent_le` over TauCeti/ returns only the declaration at Yosida.lean:316; Dense.lean:38 defines `K : ℝ := |C| + ‖g‖ + 1`, needing no nonnegativity of `C`.
findings.fix: Delete `nonneg_of_norm_resolvent_le`; if a later PR needs `0 ≤ M`, it is `(norm_nonneg _).trans (hbound 1 one_pos)` inline.
findings.issue: `nonneg_of_norm_resolvent_le` has no consumer anywhere in the repository; it is a two-line wrapper around `norm_nonneg (LinearPMap.resolvent A 1)` composed with `hbound 1 one_pos`. Its stated purpose (positivity of `M + 1` in the density argument) does not arise, since `ContinuousLinearMap.tendsto_apply_of_dense` builds its constant as `|C| + ‖g‖ + 1`.

summary: The new density-extension lemmas are genuinely absent from Mathlib (its Ascoli file still lists the dense-subset statement as a TODO), but the PR adds a domain-vector Hille--Yosida lemma that its own whole-space sibling directly subsumes, duplicates the m-dissipative specialization inline at three call sites instead of keeping the one-line `IsMDissipative` wrappers, and adds an unused nonnegativity wrapper.
